prompt.en:
There are `n` places numbered `0` to `n - 1` and two-way `roads`, each `[a, b, length]`. Each query `[start, goal, limit]` asks: can you get from `start` to `goal` using only roads strictly shorter than `limit`? Return one boolean per query, in the order given. A place always reaches itself.

There can be thousands of roads and queries, so a fresh search for every query is too slow. Several roads may join the same pair, and a road may loop back to its own place.
prompt.es:
Hay `n` lugares numerados de `0` a `n - 1` y caminos de doble sentido `roads`, cada uno `[a, b, length]`. Cada consulta `[start, goal, limit]` pregunta: ¿puedes ir de `start` a `goal` usando solo caminos de largo estrictamente menor que `limit`? Devuelve un booleano por consulta, en el orden dado. Un lugar siempre se alcanza a sí mismo.

Puede haber miles de caminos y consultas, así que una búsqueda nueva por cada consulta es demasiado lenta. Varios caminos pueden unir el mismo par, y un camino puede volver a su propio lugar.

hints.en: A search per query repeats nearly the same work every time. Notice that a higher limit only ever adds roads, and adding is exactly what union-find does well.
hints.es: Una búsqueda por consulta repite casi el mismo trabajo cada vez. Fíjate en que un límite más alto solo agrega caminos, y agregar es justo lo que union-find hace bien.

hints.en: Answer offline: sort the roads by length and the queries by limit. Before answering a query, union every road shorter than its limit that is not open yet; then compare `find(start)` and `find(goal)`.
hints.es: Responde offline: ordena los caminos por largo y las consultas por límite. Antes de responder una consulta, une cada camino más corto que su límite que aún no esté abierto; luego compara `find(start)` y `find(goal)`.

hints.en: A pointer into the sorted roads only moves forward, so each road is opened once in total. Sort the query indexes, not the queries, so every answer goes back to its original position.
hints.es: Un puntero sobre los caminos ordenados solo avanza, así que cada camino se abre una sola vez en total. Ordena los índices de las consultas, no las consultas, para que cada respuesta vuelva a su posición original.

solution:
def reachable_below(n: int, roads: list[list[int]], queries: list[list[int]]) -> list[bool]:
    parent, size = list(range(n)), [1] * n

    def find(x: int) -> int:
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]        # path halving
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    roads = sorted(roads, key=lambda road: road[2])
    answers, i = [False] * len(queries), 0
    for q in sorted(range(len(queries)), key=lambda q: queries[q][2]):    # smallest limit first
        start, goal, limit = queries[q]
        while i < len(roads) and roads[i][2] < limit:      # open every road shorter than this limit
            ra, rb = find(roads[i][0]), find(roads[i][1])
            if ra != rb:
                if size[ra] < size[rb]:
                    ra, rb = rb, ra
                parent[rb] = ra
                size[ra] += size[rb]
            i += 1
        answers[q] = find(start) == find(goal)              # answer in the original order
    return answers

complexity.time: O(E log E + Q log Q + (E + Q)·α(n)), E roads, Q queries

explain.en: A higher limit only adds roads, and union-find handles additions well. So answer the queries offline: sort them by limit, sweep the roads in order of length, and union each road as soon as the current limit exceeds it; a query is then just `find(start) == find(goal)`. Every road is unioned once in total instead of once per query. Traps: the limit is strict (a road of length `limit` stays closed), and sorting the queries themselves loses their order: sort their indexes and write each answer back.
explain.es: Un límite más alto solo agrega caminos, y union-find maneja bien las adiciones. Así que responde las consultas offline: ordénalas por límite, recorre los caminos por largo y une cada camino apenas el límite actual lo supera; una consulta es entonces solo `find(start) == find(goal)`. Cada camino se une una sola vez en total, no una vez por consulta. Trampas: el límite es estricto (un camino de largo `limit` sigue cerrado), y ordenar las consultas mismas pierde su orden: ordena sus índices y escribe cada respuesta en su lugar.

perf.gen:
import random


def gen():
    rng, n = random.Random(9), 2000
    roads = [[i, i + 1, rng.randint(1, 1000)] for i in range(n - 2)]          # a long chain; place n - 1 is cut off
    roads += [[rng.randrange(n - 1), rng.randrange(n - 1), rng.randint(1, 1000)] for _ in range(2000)]
    rng.shuffle(roads)
    queries = [[rng.randrange(n - 1), n - 1 if k % 2 else rng.randrange(n - 1), rng.randint(900, 1001)] for k in range(1000)]
    return [n, roads, queries]
perf.naive:
def reachable_below(n: int, roads: list[list[int]], queries: list[list[int]]) -> list[bool]:
    graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for a, b, length in roads:
        graph[a].append((b, length))
        graph[b].append((a, length))
    answers = []
    for start, goal, limit in queries:            # a fresh search for every query
        seen, stack = {start}, [start]
        while stack and goal not in seen:          # stop as soon as the goal is reached
            for nxt, length in graph[stack.pop()]:
                if length < limit and nxt not in seen:
                    seen.add(nxt)
                    stack.append(nxt)
        answers.append(goal in seen)
    return answers
